explanations.explanation: Priests it is, friend. Numbers 3:3 calls Aaron's sons "the anointed priests, who were ordained to serve as priests." Anointed and ordained, so this wasn't a side gig they picked up on a slow week. It was the job they were set apart for.

Judges are a real job in Israel's story, but that's not what this verse says. Numbers 3:3 says Aaron's sons were "the anointed priests, who were ordained to serve as priests." The word is priests, anointed and ordained. Nobody here is banging a gavel.
Kings, huh? Big dreams, friend, I respect that. But Numbers 3:3 says these four were "the anointed priests, who were ordained to serve as priests." No crowns in this verse, just a calling to serve.

That's the one. Numbers 3:4 says Nadab and Abihu died in the presence of the LORD "when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD in the Wilderness of Sinai." This is a heavy part of the story, and I think it's okay to let it be heavy. The text says what happened, so we let it stand.

I see why holy things come to mind here, but the ark isn't in this verse. Numbers 3:4 says Nadab and Abihu died when they "offered unauthorized fire before the LORD." It's a heavy moment, so I'll keep to what the text says.

No idol shows up in this verse, friend. Numbers 3:4 says they died when they "offered unauthorized fire before the LORD in the Wilderness of Sinai." It's a sad part of the story. I think the best thing is to read it just as it's written.

Close, but the text says the opposite. Numbers 3:4 says "they had no sons," so nobody from their line was there to step in. Only Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests during their father Aaron's lifetime. It's a quiet, sad detail, and it's worth noticing.
False is right, friend. Numbers 3:4 says Nadab and Abihu "had no sons." That's why only Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests while their father Aaron was alive. No sons, no stand-ins from that line.

I get why it sounds that way, but that's not what the text says. In Numbers 3:6 the LORD says to present the Levites to Aaron the priest "to assist him." Assist, not replace. Aaron is still the priest, and he's just getting a whole tribe of helpers.

False is right on the money. The LORD tells Moses to present the tribe of Levi to Aaron "to assist him" (Numbers 3:6). Helpers, not heirs. Aaron keeps the priesthood, and the Levites come alongside him.

explanations.answer: The furnishings of the Tent of Meeting
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. Numbers 3:8 says the Levites "shall take care of all the furnishings of the Tent of Meeting." Think of it as keeping every piece in its place. Quite the inventory list, and they were trusted with all of it.
No weapons in this job description, friend. Numbers 3:8 says the Levites "shall take care of all the furnishings of the Tent of Meeting." Their work is at the tabernacle, not the armory.

explanations.answer: The flocks and herds of Israel
explanations.explanation: Nice try, but no livestock duty here. Numbers 3:8 says the Levites "shall take care of all the furnishings of the Tent of Meeting." That's the tabernacle's things, not the pasture. Nobody's handing the Levites a shepherd's staff in this verse.

Not quite, friend. Numbers 3:10 says "any outsider who approaches the tabernacle must be put to death." The LORD gives the priesthood duties to Aaron and his sons. So no walk-ups, and that's a serious line.

False, and the text is plain about it. Numbers 3:10 says Aaron and his sons carry out the duties of the priesthood, "but any outsider who approaches the tabernacle must be put to death." The tabernacle wasn't open for anybody to wander up to.

Firstborn, yes. The LORD says, "I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel in place of every firstborn Israelite from the womb" (Numbers 3:12). The Levites stand in for the firstborn. That's the whole idea behind this chapter.

Youngest is a good guess, friend, but that's not the word. Numbers 3:12 says the Levites were taken "in place of every firstborn Israelite from the womb." It's about the firstborn, not the baby of the family.

Marriage doesn't come up in this verse. Numbers 3:12 says the LORD took the Levites "in place of every firstborn Israelite from the womb." The word is firstborn. Whether a person was married never enters into it.

That's right. The LORD says, "On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to Myself all the firstborn in Israel" (Numbers 3:13). Both things happen on the same day. It's a serious memory, and He is the one pointing back to it.

explanations.answer: Parted the waters of the sea
explanations.explanation: The sea parting is a real event, but it isn't what the LORD points to here. In Numbers 3:13 He says, "On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to Myself all the firstborn in Israel." That's the day He means.

The tablets are real, but they aren't what this verse is about. Numbers 3:13 says, "On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I consecrated to Myself all the firstborn in Israel." The day in Egypt is the one the LORD points back to.

True, friend. The LORD says He consecrated all the firstborn in Israel, "both man and beast" (Numbers 3:13). So the animals count too, along with the people. Then He adds, "They are Mine; I am the LORD."
Look again at the end of the verse. The LORD says He consecrated all the firstborn in Israel, "both man and beast" (Numbers 3:13). So the animals are included along with the people.

explanations.answer: Every male a month old or more
explanations.explanation: Yes, friend. The LORD says, "You are to count every male a month old or more" (Numbers 3:15). That reaches all the way down to the babies. It's a much wider count than only the grown men.

Twenty is a number you may have heard for counting, but not in this verse. The LORD says, "You are to count every male a month old or more" (Numbers 3:15). That means the babies are in the count, too.
This count isn't about fighting, friend. The LORD says, "You are to count every male a month old or more" (Numbers 3:15). A one-month-old isn't swinging a sword, and he's still on the list.

explanations.answer: Perform the duties of the sanctuary
explanations.explanation: That's it. Numbers 3:38 says Moses, Aaron and Aaron's sons "were to perform the duties of the sanctuary as a service on behalf of the Israelites." They camp on the east, toward the sunrise, right in front of the Tent of Meeting. It's a front-row spot for the work.
Settling disputes isn't in this verse, friend. Numbers 3:38 says they "were to perform the duties of the sanctuary as a service on behalf of the Israelites." Their work here is at the sanctuary.

explanations.answer: Guard the gates of the camp
explanations.explanation: Gate duty isn't what the text says. Numbers 3:38 says Moses, Aaron and Aaron's sons "were to perform the duties of the sanctuary as a service on behalf of the Israelites." The sanctuary is where their duties are.

True, friend. The LORD tells Moses to take "the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the livestock of the Israelites" (Numbers 3:41). So the animals get a swap too. The people and their livestock are both covered.

Check the end of that verse. The LORD says to take the Levites for Him "and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the livestock of the Israelites" (Numbers 3:41). So the livestock swap really happens, right alongside the people.
Right. The firstborn males came to 22,273, and the Levites were 22,000 (Numbers 3:43, 39). So the firstborn outnumber the Levites. There's a gap, and the LORD gives Moses a plan for it.

A perfect match would've been tidy, friend, but the numbers don't line up. The firstborn males were 22,273 and the Levites were 22,000 (Numbers 3:43, 39). That leaves a gap, and the LORD gives Moses a plan for it.

It goes the other direction. The firstborn males came to 22,273, while the Levites came to 22,000 (Numbers 3:43, 39). So the firstborn are the bigger group. That's why the LORD talks about redeeming the extra ones.

Five shekels is it. The LORD says, "you are to collect five shekels for each one, according to the sanctuary shekel of twenty gerahs" (Numbers 3:47). It's a set price for each one. The price is just what the LORD said.
That's ten times too much, friend. The LORD says, "you are to collect five shekels for each one, according to the sanctuary shekel of twenty gerahs" (Numbers 3:47). It's five, not fifty.

Thirty is a number that turns up elsewhere in the Bible, but not here. The LORD says, "you are to collect five shekels for each one, according to the sanctuary shekel of twenty gerahs" (Numbers 3:47). In this passage the price is five.

Aaron is right for the first blank. The LORD says, "Give the money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for the excess among the Israelites" (Numbers 3:48). Aaron is the priest, and the money goes to him.
Sons is right for the second blank. The LORD says, "Give the money to Aaron and his sons" (Numbers 3:48). So the money goes to Aaron and to his sons together.

Moses is the one doing the collecting, friend, not the one receiving. The LORD says, "Give the money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for the excess among the Israelites" (Numbers 3:48). Moses hands it off and keeps none of it.
Brothers is a reasonable guess, but it isn't the word. The LORD says, "Give the money to Aaron and his sons" (Numbers 3:48). It's his sons, the same family of priests.

The elders aren't mentioned in this verse. The LORD says, "Give the money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for the excess among the Israelites" (Numbers 3:48). The money goes to Aaron and his sons, and no one else gets a share.
Not quite, friend. Numbers 3:49 says Moses collected money "from those in excess of the number redeemed by the Levites." That's only the 273 extra ones. The Levites already stood in for the rest.

False is right. Moses collected the redemption money "from those in excess of the number redeemed by the Levites" (Numbers 3:49). That's the 273 extra firstborn, not all 22,273. The Levites already covered the rest.
